japan1.title: 「スペースX」が上場 調達資金 約12兆円は過去最大規模
japan1.description: アメリカの実業家、イーロン・マスク氏が率い、宇宙開発やAI事業を手がける「スペースX」は12日、ニューヨークのナスダック市場に上場しました。上場による調達額はおよそ750億ドル、日本円にしておよそ12兆円と過去最大の規模となります。

japan1.title: ウリ信用組合に一部業務停止命令 顧客の預金着服などで 金融庁
japan1.description: 金融庁は、札幌市のウリ信用組合に対して、元役員が顧客の預金を着服するなど複数の不祥事が起きていたにもかかわらず、長期間にわたり経営陣の主導で隠蔽していたなどとして、12日、新規顧客への貸し付けなど一部業務の停止命令を出しました。

japan1.title: 大手航空2社 燃油サーチャージ再度引き上げ 燃料価格高騰で
japan1.description: 全日空と日本航空は、国際線の運賃に上乗せする燃油サーチャージについて、7月の発券分から引き上げると発表しました。5月と6月の発券分も引き上げていましたが、燃料の高騰が続いていることを受けての対応だとしています。

japan1.title: Booking.comの予約客に不審なメッセージ相次ぐ 注意呼びかけ
japan1.description: 日本ホテル協会は、宿泊予約サイト「Booking.com」を通じてホテルを予約した客に、クレジットカードの情報を入力させようとする不審なメッセージが届く事例が相次いでいるとして、注意を呼びかけています。

japan1.title: 円相場 小幅な値動き 1ドル＝160円台前半での取り引き
japan1.description: 12日の東京外国為替市場、円相場は小幅な値動きとなり、1ドル＝160円台前半での取り引きが続きました。

japan1.title: スーパーのコメ平均価格 5キロ 税込み3644円 3週連続値下がり
japan1.description: 全国のスーパーで6月7日までの1週間に販売されたコメの平均価格は、5キロ当たり税込み3644円と前の週より29円下がりました。値下がりは3週連続で、銘柄米の下げ幅が大きくなっています。

japan1.title: 生命保険の営業職員 新たな呼び名は「ソナエルジュ」に
japan1.description: 家庭や職場を訪れて保険を販売し、生保レディーとも呼ばれた営業職員について、生命保険協会は、新たな呼び名を「ソナエルジュ」にすると発表しました。性別にとらわれず、顧客に寄り添うという仕事内容が表現されているとしています。

japan1.title: 自民対策本部 南米EPA交渉なら“農業に配慮を”政府に申し入れ
japan1.description: 南米の関税同盟「メルコスール」と日本との間のEPA＝経済連携協定について、自民党の対策本部は仮に交渉を始める場合、国内農業への影響を避けるため、牛肉をはじめとした重要な品目に十分配慮することなどを政府に申し入れました。

japan1.title: 株価 一時2800円超上昇 イランへの攻撃中止表明受け
japan1.description: 12日の東京株式市場、アメリカのトランプ大統領がイランへの攻撃を中止したと明らかにしたことなどを受けて、日経平均株価の上昇幅は一時、2800円を超えました。

japan1.title: 東京株式市場 キオクシアHDの時価総額が国内首位に
japan1.description: 12日の東京株式市場で、半導体・フラッシュメモリの世界大手、キオクシアホールディングスの株価が上昇し、時価総額がトヨタ自動車を上回って国内首位になりました。

japan1.title: “来月 原油代替調達で去年並み確保も対策進める”経産相
japan1.description: ホルムズ海峡を経由しない代替ルートでの原油の調達で来月は中東情勢が悪化する前の去年とほぼ同じ量を確保できる見込みとなったことについて、赤澤経済産業大臣は12日の閣議のあとの会見で、必要な量の確保など原油の安定供給に向けた対策を引き続き進めていく考えを示しました。

japan1.title: 改正郵便法が成立 郵便料金を柔軟に変更可能に 値上げも検討
japan1.description: 日本郵便で郵便事業の赤字が続いていることを受けて、料金を総務大臣の認可によって改定できるようにする郵便法の改正案が、12日開かれた参議院本会議で可決・成立しました。

aus1.title: 'Special player and person': NZ cricket legend Williamson retires
aus1.description: New Zealand cricketing legend Kane Williamson announces his retirement from the game immediately after a stunning career.

aus1.title: Sam Short equals Grant Hackett and reminds us how far we've come
aus1.description: Sam Short wins the 200m, 400m, 800m and 1,500m national titles to equal the feats of Grant Hackett more than 20 years ago.

aus1.title: Taylor Swift, Alanis Morissette inducted into Songwriters Hall of Fame
aus1.description: Taylor Swift has become the youngest woman to be inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. She's among the writers behind some of pop's biggest hits to be inducted in 2026.

aus1.title: Meet the mullet-bearing drag kings of Hobart lip-syncing about Centrelink
aus1.description: Hobart's drag kings say the closure of a gay bar pushed their performances into heteronormative spaces and a surprisingly accepting Tasmanian community.

aus1.title: As work modernises in Australia, some rare trades are in decline
aus1.description: A shortage of locksmiths in Australia persists despite government-funded incentives. The nation's changing labour landscape has meant some specialist trades are not being chosen by apprentices.

aus1.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX takes off, worth more than $2.8 trillion
aus1.description: SpaceX shares began trading for about $150 each, 11 per cent higher than the $135 estimate.

aus1.title: Trump says ceasefire deal 'close', but it could be on Iran's terms
aus1.description: Amid rising expectations a pathway to peace between Iran and the US is close, the reported details of a ceasefire deal appear to show Iran getting numerous concessions from the White House.

aus1.title: Heated Rivalry, Off Campus driving ice hockey boom
aus1.description: Women now outnumber men as attendees to Canberra Brave ice hockey games — thanks in part to a surge in popularity for the sport inspired by the recent shows Heated Rivalry and Off Campus.

aus1.title: These fawning, faux-friendly celebrity interviews make my teeth ache
aus1.description: Why is it that every interviewer now feels they must arrive to their four-minute-long encounter with a gift, a scrapbook, or a movie stub they've hung onto for decades?

aus1.title: After 18,500 hours of free counselling, pop-up centres are closing
aus1.description: Set up in the wake of 2022's catastrophic floods, these drop-in mental health centres in the Northern Rivers are shutting down.

aus1.title: SANFL players consider industrial action as hourly salary drops to $8
aus1.description: The SANFL Players' Association is discussing the potential of a strike in response to a 50 per cent decline in pay over the past 20 years.

aus1.title: Booming protein powder market opens doors for food manufacturers
aus1.description: A Queensland food manufacturer turns second-grade peanuts into high-protein powder as demand for protein-enhanced foods grows in Australia and overseas.

aus1.title: 'A footballer's dream': From humble beginings to the world stage
aus1.description: The Touré brothers snuck into their local football field after hours to play the game they loved, while the Yengi brothers kicked around makeshift balls made of plastic bags. Two of them have now made it onto the world stage as Socceroos.

aus1.title: 'Difficult period': Top NRL ref confirms he had gambling problem
aus1.description: Origin referee Ashley Klein has confirmed he battled with a gambling addiction after a report claimed he lost $400,000.

aus1.title: How Israel's operation 'Eternal Darkness' in southern Lebanon is expanding
aus1.description: The so-called ceasefire since April, which Hezbollah is not a party to, has done little to halt the death and destruction in southern Lebanon. Here's how the scale of the Israeli operation called "Eternal Darkness" continues to expand.

aus1.title: Paper trail tracks alleged downfall of Parramatta's Pink Ladies
aus1.description: Over the past five weeks, emotional hearings at the inquiry into alleged corruption at the City of Parramatta have contained bombshell admissions and insights.

aus1.title: From Southbank to the Skyneedle: The legacies of Australia's biggest event
aus1.description: Expo '88 took over Brisbane in 1988, turning the southern banks of the Brisbane River into a multi-national bonanza. What legacy did it leave behind?

aus1.title: A man fled a 'bounty' in Canberra. Months later, he was dead in Brisbane
aus1.description: Neil Tracey's death was ruled an overdose in what investigators would call an open and shut case. His family are questioning if police knew about the bounty that led him to flee his hometown.

aus1.title: Grandfather of child rescued from Syria pleads for 'stability, love, care'
aus1.description: Jasmine was five years old and so traumatised that when she woke up trying to scream, she couldn't make a sound.

aus1.title: Feral sambar deer likely brought to SA for hunting purposes
aus1.description: One of Australia's largest feral deer species was spotted in SA's Riverland for the first time earlier this month. While its existence is being investigated, the Invasive Species Council says it was likely transported across state lines for hunting purposes.

aus1.title: The sword that links feared pirates to Britain's greatest naval hero
aus1.description: The history of a wavy-bladed sword, bought at a Brisbane gun show around the end of the 1980s, begins with Moro raiders resisting Spanish colonists in the Philippines, but may also include Admiral Lord Nelson.

aus1.title: Reuben Kaye reckons you can joke about anything — 'it's just how you do it'
aus1.description: The new artistic director of the Adelaide Cabaret Festival shares what's unique about the art form in Australia and what his teenage self would think about who he is today.

aus1.title: Why we cannot name the high-profile man at the centre of an extortion case
aus1.description: There is a highly secretive and unusual court case playing out behind closed doors in Far North Queensland involving a prominent married man and his alleged affair, a non-publication order we are not allowed to see and an allegation of extortion we cannot tell you much about.

aus1.title: New ambassador to US takes up tariffs, AUKUS causes
aus1.description: Greg Moriarty says he will "robustly" push back on the Trump administration's "extremely disappointing" new tariff plan and may recruit Australian businesses to help take up the fight.

aus1.title: Farmers worry 70km dingo fence 'not enough' to protect sheep
aus1.description: Farmers in Victoria’s north-west say a new dingo exclusion fence will only push the problem of livestock predation onto their neighbours.

bang3.title: Need 1 week to assess situation
bang3.description: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

bang3.title: Wasfia 1st Bangladeshi to conquer K2
bang3.description: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

bang3.title: CU admin identifies 2 molesters
bang3.description: The administration of Chittagong University yesterday claimed to have identified two persons who sexually assaulted a female student on the campus on Sunday night.

bang3.title: Rohingya genocide case to proceed
bang3.description: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

bang3.title: CU sexual assault: Fingers pointed at BCL men
bang3.description: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

bang3.title: Noab hikes newspaper price by Tk 2 from Jul 25
bang3.description: All newspapers owned by the members of Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (Noab) will see a price increase of at least Tk 2 per issue from July 25.

bang3.title: Yet-to-start mega projects: Consider putting  them on hold
bang3.description: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

bang3.title: ‘You cannot remain silent’
bang3.description: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

bang3.title: Electricity crisis may worsen
bang3.description: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

bang3.title: EC’s dialogue hits a snag as BNP skips it
bang3.description: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.
